cases.input_abstraction: An emotionally important separation/triage exchange consists mostly of terse functional question-answer turns. Facts and motives are correct, but little pressure, conflicting desire, embodied resistance or aftershock is dramatized.
A character in immediate danger packages mission fact, external spread, reward value and arrival evidence into one polished explanatory speech despite shared context.

A named supporting character previously withdrew, later returns to the active scene and changes function, but no located new perception, report, obligation or continuing causal trigger supports the return.

A manuscript contains many attacks, arrivals and revelations, but major spans do not strengthen reader expectation and the climax does not progressively compress meaningful options or make stakes more personal.

A strange recurring projectile appears several times; characters note that it is odd and later an antagonist explains the scheme. Before payoff, the reader has little supported working hypothesis, verification action or model-changing contradiction.
Very short task dialogue directly allocates action under physical constraint and each turn changes an immediate choice.
Very short memorial dialogue is anchored to a unique shared object, deceased relationship and ritual, and changes grief/relationship reading.
A quiet scene has little external action but increases dread and forces a meaningful private choice.
A formal briefing delivers complete information because the speaker has an explicit briefing duty, adequate time and an audience that needs the package.
